title: Reverse Linked List II
description: Reverse the nodes of a singly linked list from position left to position right, using one-based indexing, and return the resulting list.
inputFormat: Second line: n space-separated node values
Third line: integers left and right
outputFormat: Print the resulting linked list values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Nodes from positions 2 through 4 are reversed.

title: Remove Nth Node From End
description: Remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list and return the remaining list.
outputFormat: Print the remaining linked list values separated by spaces. Print EMPTY if no nodes remain.

examples.explanation: The second node from the end contains 4.

title: Add Two Numbers
description: Two non-empty linked lists represent non-negative integers in reverse digit order. Add them and return the result as a reversed linked list.
outputFormat: Print the result digits in reverse order separated by spaces.
constraints: No leading zero except for zero itself

title: Reorder List
description: Reorder a linked list from L0 â†’ L1 â†’ ... â†’ Ln into L0 â†’ Ln â†’ L1 â†’ Ln-1 â†’ L2 â†’ Ln-2 and so on.
inputFormat: Second line: n linked list values
outputFormat: Print the reordered list values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Take alternately from the front and the back.

title: Linked List Cycle II
description: Return the zero-based index of the node where a linked-list cycle begins. Return -1 if the list has no cycle.
inputFormat: Third line: integer pos, the index connected to by the last node, or -1

examples.explanation: The tail connects to the node at index 1.

title: Copy List with Random Pointer
description: Create a deep copy of a linked list in which each node has next and random pointers. The random pointer may point to any node or null.
inputFormat: Third line: n integers representing random-pointer indices, where -1 means null
outputFormat: Print copied values on one line and copied random indices on the next line.

examples.explanation: The copied list has identical values and random relationships but new nodes.

title: LRU Cache
description: Design a Least Recently Used cache supporting get and put operations in average O(1) time.
inputFormat: First line: capacity and number of operations
Next lines: GET key or PUT key value
outputFormat: For every GET operation, print the returned value on its own line.

examples.input:
2 9
PUT 1 1
PUT 2 2
GET 1
PUT 3 3
GET 2
PUT 4 4
GET 1
GET 3
GET 4
examples.explanation: Least-recently-used entries are evicted when capacity is exceeded.

title: Reverse Nodes in K Group
description: Reverse linked-list nodes in consecutive groups of size k. Leave the final group unchanged if it contains fewer than k nodes.
inputFormat: First line: integers n and k
Second line: n linked list values
outputFormat: Print the resulting list values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Each complete group of two nodes is reversed.

title: Merge K Sorted Lists
description: Merge k individually sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list.
inputFormat: For each list: one line with its length followed by its sorted values
outputFormat: Print all merged values in non-decreasing order. Print EMPTY when all lists are empty.

examples.explanation: All nodes are merged in sorted order.

title: Sort List
description: Sort a linked list in ascending order using O(n log n) time. Prefer constant or logarithmic auxiliary space.
inputFormat: Second line: n linked list values
outputFormat: Print the sorted values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: The nodes are sorted by value.
